nodes: Factorization analysis: iteratively test and repair a decomposition rather than assuming its categories are primitive.
When should factorization analysis be activated in planning or inquiry?
Activate factorization analysis when an alternative decomposition could change a material downstream decision.
What is megamodeling, and is it relevant to the inquiry formalism?
Megamodeling / Global Model Management as prior art for representing models/artifacts and their relationships.
Megamodeling asks what representations/artifacts exist, what kinds they are, and how they relate.
Factorization analysis asks whether a particular representation is decomposed appropriately for the active decision.
Reasoning may reduce to mathematics and logic conditional on the rules/conditions of the game being modeled.
How can an embedded observer determine what kind of game or formalism it is in?
An embedded observer cannot simply assume it knows which game it is playing.
The game/formalism itself should be represented as a hypothesis.
Global metaphysical certainty may remain unavailable while inquiry proceeds conditionally.
The practical target can be local, conditional, operational adequacy rather than global metaphysical certainty.
Defining the structure of the game should be separated from choosing an optimal strategy within it.
A modeled agent can hold beliefs or philosophical commitments that differ from the analyst's truth or optimality judgments.
Define the descriptive space of possible games before solving for optimal play.
Chess illustrates the distinction between specifying board/pieces/legal moves and solving how to beat a strong opponent.
Game description and strategy/optimization are separate modeling problems.
A game description has a formal/logical side and an external-reality side whose adequacy must be learned indirectly.
Formal consequence within a model does not by itself establish empirical adequacy of that model for external reality.
Uncertainty among known possible rule sets.
Failure to represent or conceive some possible rules/actions at all.
Unknown rulebook versus discovering an unrepresented move such as castling.
Construct a white-box simulation and place embedded resource-limited agents inside it for controlled formal study.
An embedded agent with bounded information, representation, and computation.
God-level simulator access can reveal the true rules/state without making all consequences computationally cheap.
Even with a known white-box model, computational irreducibility or intractability can block efficient consequence prediction.
Knowing exact rules does not imply tractable access to the full game tree or consequences.
Which established formalisms already cover unknown, partially conceived, reactive, resource-bounded games?
Games with unawareness and discovery as prior art for agents whose subjective game can expand through interaction.
Reuse established game, learning, unawareness, control, and systems formalisms before inventing a new generalized game tuple.
Is compositional game theory relevant to the structure of possible games?
Compositional game theory / open games as prior art for composing game components through interfaces.
Compositional game theory is especially relevant to the question of what a game is made of.
A subsystem need not intrinsically be an Agent; strategic semantics can be a modeling layer on an open component.
Open/categorical systems, compositional games, unawareness/discovery, and bounded reasoning form a close prior-art stack for the problem.
Compositionality may structure the space of games before strategy or optimality is introduced.
Record this continuation as a source-grounded Inquiry Graph trajectory.
Make the base notion of game deliberately broad enough to include essentially all lawful systems, while preserving meaning through typed enrichments.
Game/non-game and intelligence/non-intelligence may be misleading binary partitions; graded structure and competence are preferred.
Competence may grade down to very simple or even physical systems rather than beginning at a sharp agency threshold.
A ball rolling downhill is proposed as a degenerate competence/game case governed by physical dynamics rather than deliberation.
If every lawful process is called a game, the term risks collapsing into a synonym for process.
Test whether game theory can be expanded downward from rich strategic cases to passive and scientific-interaction cases.
Scientific inquiry can be modeled as interaction with a non-strategically-reactive system whose dynamics generate responses to observations/interventions.
Start from rich game theory and remove unnecessary assumptions rather than building upward from a minimal process formalism.
Process/dynamics may be the least enriched case of a more general game object.
A sufficiently rich system can model the external world, itself within that world, and a goal attributed to that modeled self.
A system's own represented goal is not automatically epistemically privileged over external observer or white-box descriptions.
White-box and black-box distinguish analyst access rather than defining different kinds of systems or research arms.
White-box, observer-inferred, and self-attributed goal descriptions need not coincide.
Collective Competence ontology as the existing authority for goal criteria, access contracts, provenance, competence, boundary, and scale distinctions.
The approved prior-art pass found that open games already admit surprisingly degenerate cases, reducing the need for a homemade universal-game tuple.
Open games with agency separate compositional arena/interaction structure from optional selection/evaluation semantics.
How can composition, perspectival goals/self-models, changing awareness, and resource-bounded computation be connected without losing their native semantics?
Construct a paper-level translation contract for a bounded self-model case plus a passive component before adding implementation.
What is the current status of the universal-game investigation after the approved prior-art pass?
Update Inquiry Graph with this continuation and then proceed to the translation-contract research step.
Is entertaining or selecting a game a distinct formal problem, or is it already covered by decision theory and hypothesis generation?
The game a system is effectively playing depends jointly on what it wants and on hypotheses about how its actions lead to outcomes.
Game selection may be derived from existing decision-theoretic and hypothesis-generation machinery rather than requiring a new foundational layer.
Prefer mature off-the-shelf systems over novelty or bespoke infrastructure when they adequately satisfy the actual need.
Should generalized infrastructure be selected primarily by first-principles architecture and state-of-the-art evidence rather than by long multi-framework bake-offs?
Most generalized infrastructure choices can be settled from architecture, economics, and mature framework capabilities, reserving experiments for residual uncertainties.
Behavioral simulation, feasibility/optimization, and strategic analysis are distinct concerns that can map to Concordia-like agents, optimization solvers, and compositional game theory respectively.
What role, if any, should compositional game theory retain in the generalized architecture?
Long-range dependencies and constraints should propagate through explicit world mechanics rather than being reconstructed inside each agent decision.
Truck fuel feasibility is a mechanically propagated constraint that should not depend on an agent remembering the entire logistics world in context.
Small composable units can encode local constraints and causal propagation and then be wired into larger interdependent worlds.
The desired compositionality is primarily a compositional causal/mechanical world model; compositional game theory applies only to components with genuinely strategic semantics.
World causal structure should live in reusable executable components rather than in an agent prompt or model context.
The composed executable world is primary; agents are one class of participant or policy interacting with it rather than the substrate itself.

A compositional world may contain heterogeneous component semantics—deterministic mechanics, dynamical processes, optimization models, probabilistic mechanisms, open games, and agent policies—connected through explicit interfaces.
An open game should be one composable component type among others, not the formalism forced onto the whole world.
Build complex worlds compositionally from small explicit executable units so dependencies propagate structurally rather than through agent memory or inference.
Compositional game theory remains valuable as the strategic semantics for components whose outcomes depend on incentives, beliefs, observations, and anticipated responses.
What is the smallest common interface that lets mechanical, dynamical, strategic, optimization, probabilistic, and agentic components compose without erasing their native semantics?
Extend the existing operational-games Inquiry Graph with the replacement-first and compositional-world continuation rather than creating a duplicate graph.
Which game/model to entertain is coupled to the current objective and hypotheses about how actions lead to outcomes, rather than being an isolated game-selection primitive.
Candidate generation already has substantial mature prior art and should not be reopened as an undefined foundational gap.
Bring the project documentation into a coherent, current, consistent, well-organized and compendious state, updating or archiving obsolete information.
Has the documentation/update workflow become stuck?
